papers.title: The point-cross dimension
papers.abstract: Two transverse segments have local Hausdorff and upper box dimension one at their crossing, although they carry two independent tangent directions. We define the Point-Cross Dimension by assigning each tangent line the largest local upper box dimension captured by intersection with a regular \(C^1\) curve in that direction, then taking the supremum of their sums over finite independent families of tangent lines. Every Bouligand direction admits such a recurrent curve. The resulting profile is invariant under closure and covariant under local \(C^1\)-diffeomorphisms. Each directional weight is attained, and the profile is upper semicontinuous. An integral representation by ranks of weight superlevel sets gives submodularity and, together with projection bounds, exact Cartesian-product additivity. Germs with the same projective tangent support, local upper box dimension, and rank of segment directions can have different Point-Cross Dimensions. Further computations give exact directional profiles for chirps and the Point-Cross Dimension of a self-affine carpet. Finally, approximation of a ray with error \(O(t^d)\), for \(d>1\), forces directional weight at least \(1-1/d\), and this bound is sharp.

papers.title: On the Complexity of Finding Fixed Points for Set-Valued Contractions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the computational complexity of finding fixed points for set-valued contractions. We first formulate a computational problem for Nadler's fixed-point theorem: Projected-Nadler, and prove that it is $\mathsf{CLS}$-complete by showing its equivalence to Continuous-LocalOpt. We then establish a stronger converse for Nadler's fixed point theorem that can be applied as a tool to analyze the convergence rate of set-valued basic iteration procedure. Finally, we reduce large-margin triplet stationarity problem to Projected-Nadler. Together with its $\mathsf{CLS}$-hardness introduced in [arXiv:2509.16898], this yields $\mathsf{CLS}$-completeness of large-margin triplet stationarity.

papers.title: Duality and Baire like properties in topological abelian groups
papers.abstract: This article investigates the duality of abelian topological groups by delving into the interplay between the algebraic and topological properties of a group $G$ and those of its dual group. In particular, extending the notion of a $g$-barrelled group, we introduce and study the classes of $\kappa$-barrelled and $\omega$-barrelled groups. Our first main result establishes that every $\omega$-barrelled group is $\aleph_0$-barrelled (i.e., if every weakly convergent sequence in the dual group is equicontinuous, then every metrizable weakly compact subset of the dual group is also equicontinuous). From this, we deduce that the free topological abelian group $A(K)$ over a metrizable compact space $K$ is determined by the subgroup generated by any of its dense subsets. Furthermore, we prove that if $G$ is a $\sigma$-compact, $\omega$-barrelled group, then its dual group $\widehat{G}_\kappa$ equipped with the compact-open topology is sequentially complete (complete if $G$ is hemicompact). We also solve an open question posed by Trigos-Arrieta by constructing an explicit example of an $\omega$-barrelled metrizable group that fails to be $g$-barrelled. Finally, we investigate the dualization of groups lacking infinite compact subsets, proving that for a totally bounded abelian group $G$, every compact subset of $G$ is finite if and only if its dual group $\widehat{G}$, endowed with the finite-open topology, is unordered Baire-like.
